state: Corrected preparation only. No video recording, browser/account inspection, upload, Console change, new OAuth or attestation.

supersedesForNextCapture.correction: A generic accessible video URL and blanket browser-address-bar exclusion are insufficient. Use Google’s documented upload destination/visibility and retain required public OAuth client ID evidence.

primarySources.supports: Video destination/visibility, actual English OAuth grant/consent, app identity, address-bar client ID and per-scope feature demonstration.
Meanings of calendars.readonly and events.owned; do not describe events.owned as a write-only or freebusy-only permission.
Authorization request client_id differs from confidential client_secret and returned authorization code; callback code exchange remains off camera.

officialRequirementsParaphrased: Upload the completed demonstration through YouTube Studio with Unlisted visibility; provide that video link.
Demonstrate the actual English OAuth grant and consent experience, the app name, and the consent-page address bar containing the app’s OAuth client ID.
Demonstrate what the app does with each requested sensitive permission. Include Google Sign-In only if the app uses it.

appFactsFromReadOnlyCurrentSource.appIdentity: Existing emailed-link owner session; Google OAuth separately grants Calendar access.
appFactsFromReadOnlyCurrentSource.englishPrecondition: The current authorization builder does not explicitly set hl=en. Owner/Root must confirm actual grant screens are English before capture; this preparation changes no request parameters.

scopeDemonstrations.actualAppClip: After actual grant, show the connected existing primary Calendar and its time zone/identity in the app. Do not expose another calendar’s content.

Show checked arrival-window availability and one synthetic owned visit successfully created, moved and cancelled with matching delivery status. Existing unrelated busy intervals may suppress windows but their titles/descriptions/attendee identities stay off screen.

startGate: Root diagnoses the owner’s exact current OAuth issue before another authorization request. No assumption that a missing popup, declined consent, request expiry and Google configuration errors are the same problem.
Complete source, app/provider readiness, bounded proof/capture/cleanup scope and recorder preflight before opening any new expiring handoff.
Confirm the owner is actively present and ready to complete the permission screen now. A new window is not a substitute for readiness or error diagnosis.
Use a separate fresh capture phase only after Root closes the active proof. Existing v7 timers, budgets and cleanup remain unchanged.

captureProcedure.action: Use the newly bound regular Chrome window only. Record the actual signed-in synthetic workspace, public app identity, privacy/access explanation and Connect Calendar control. Stop and await finalized-file receipt before navigation.
Capture OFF for account chooser, password, MFA and recovery. Owner handles these without recording. No agent explores other tabs/accounts. Start no consent clip while an error is unresolved.

captureProcedure.clip: English consent and public client identity
captureProcedure.action: On the exact safe stationary Google permission screen, capture app name, the full English permission descriptions and any scope selections. Include the Chrome address bar with the real client_id readable. If needed, focus the existing bar without editing/navigating to make that parameter readable. Do not replace it with a title card, mock URL or a different OAuth request.

Record every distinct permission-review page needed to explain the actual grant, including current selections and the final grant control. Stop and confirm finalization before any action that can navigate to the authorization-code callback. Owner grants while capture is OFF; disclose that cut explicitly. Do not record a callback URL even briefly.

Resume only after the same owned window returns to a normal approved app route without OAuth code/token parameters. Show the actual connected state and primary Calendar identity/time zone. Do not present a prior grant or static mock as this grant’s return.

Demonstrate actual checked availability and the same synthetic managed event’s successful create, move and cancel through the app with observed delivery results, followed by disconnect. Queued status or a refused move is not substituted for successful provider delivery. Keep unrelated personal events and the Google Calendar event grid out of capture.

Pause/finalize capture during ordinary scheduled waits and insert labelled cuts with elapsed-time context. Use reviewed clips from the same bound phase, not recreated successes. Native AVFoundation can join H264/MP4 clips without ffmpeg.

After phase cleanup, review the complete local export including every boundary frame. Confirm all shown state/nonces are consumed or expired, public client ID is readable, English grant/each scope use are understandable, and no password/MFA/code/token/client secret/personal event or unrelated window appears. Root then arranges separately authorized YouTube Studio Unlisted upload of that exact reviewed file and a reviewer-accessible link; Steve reviews the completed verification draft and any final attestation.

honestCutsConstraint.status: Proposed privacy-preserving capture design, not a Google acceptance determination.
honestCutsConstraint.officialVsInference: The official page requires a full grant demonstration but does not explicitly approve the proposed stop-before-callback editing pattern. The segmented design is our inference, not a documented exception.
honestCutsConstraint.acceptanceGate: Before upload, Root/PO must assess whether the app-entry, complete English permission review/selections/final control and actual granted return together clearly demonstrate the grant. If the cut obscures it, the video stays incomplete; prepare a separately reviewed safe method or obtain Google guidance rather than claim compliance or record credentials/callback codes.

safeRecorderReuse.priorObservation: Compile-only Swift ScreenCaptureKit/SCRecordingOutput plus AVFoundation APIs typechecked; current-context capture permission preflight was granted. No capture was started or window enumerated.
safeRecorderReuse.binding: Single-window OS picker selects only the exact newly owned regular Chrome window; do not equate AppleScript window ID and CGWindowID. No entire-display capture or other tab/window enumeration.
safeRecorderReuse.pendingImplementation: Bounded validated recorder/start-stop/finalized receipts, private output files and an authorized synthetic-window usability test are still needed.
safeRecorderReuse.noBlanketAddressBarCrop: Consent identity clip keeps the browser address bar/client ID. A callback exclusion constraint does not justify hiding required OAuth identity evidence.
